dbToolsCard.title: Export & import data
dbToolsCard.description: Move or combine outreach data between DOCENT instances. The export is a portable JSON file of institutions, venues, events, and their authors. Importing <merges>merges</merges> — records that already exist (matched by natural key) are left untouched, so re-importing never creates duplicates. This is separate from the automatic database <backups>backups</backups> below.

siteSetupCard.title: Site address & domain setup
siteSetupCard.collapsedSubtitle: — point a subdomain at this server (optional)
siteSetupCard.description: Give your instance a friendly web address like https://docent.your-org.edu. This takes two things: a DNS “A record” your IT department adds (pointing the name at your machine), and HTTPS on the server — which DOCENT already bundles. Fill in the two fields below and this panel writes the exact request to send IT and the one-line change that turns HTTPS on.
siteSetupCard.publicSiteAddressDescription: Saved with your instance and used to build the setup instructions below.
siteSetupCard.invalidAddressWarning: That doesn’t look like a valid web address — use something like https://docent.your-org.edu.
siteSetupCard.serverIpDescription: Find this in your cloud/VM console (e.g. the instance's public IPv4). Not stored — only used to fill in the request.
siteSetupCard.howItFitsTogetherBody: 1. IT creates an <strongRecord>A record</strongRecord> so <hostCode>{{host}}</hostCode> resolves to your machine’s IP, and opens ports <strongPort80>80</strongPort80> and <strongPort443>443</strongPort443>. 2. You set <domainCode>SITE_DOMAIN</domainCode> in <envCode>.env</envCode> and re-run <scriptCode>./scripts/start.sh</scriptCode> — DOCENT’s bundled <caddyLink>Caddy</caddyLink> proxy then serves HTTPS and gets a free, auto-renewing certificate. Nothing extra to install. That’s the whole setup.
siteSetupCard.requestLabel: 1 · Request to send your IT / DNS department
siteSetupCard.footerNote: Once IT confirms the record is live, add that line to <envCode>.env</envCode> and run <scriptCode>./scripts/start.sh</scriptCode> — the bundled Caddy proxy starts automatically and fetches the certificate. DNS changes can take up to an hour to take effect worldwide. Leaving <domainCode>SITE_DOMAIN</domainCode> empty keeps the app on <localhostCode>http://localhost</localhostCode> only.
siteSetupCard.dnsRequestSubject: Subject: DNS request — new A record for {{host}}
siteSetupCard.dnsRequestIntro: We're running a small self-hosted web app on our own server and would like a subdomain to point to it. Could you please create this DNS record?
siteSetupCard.dnsRequestIpv6Note: If we also have an IPv6 address, please add a matching AAAA record to it.
siteSetupCard.dnsRequestClosing: Once the record is live we'll serve the site over HTTPS — the server obtains and renews its own TLS certificate automatically, so nothing else is needed on your end. The only inbound ports the server uses are 80 and 443.
siteSetupCard.envSnippetComment: in your .env on the server, then re-run ./scripts/start.sh

analyticsCard.title: Website analytics
analyticsCard.description: See how many people visit your site — including the public impact page — without cookies or personal profiles. DOCENT supports <cfLink>Cloudflare Web Analytics</cfLink>, which is free and privacy-first. Paste the snippet Cloudflare gives you below and it loads on every page. Leave it empty to turn analytics off.
analyticsCard.howToTitle: How to get your snippet (about 2 minutes)
analyticsCard.step1: Open <dashLink>Cloudflare Web Analytics</dashLink> and sign in (create a free Cloudflare account if you don't have one — no credit card, and you do not need to move your DNS to Cloudflare).
analyticsCard.step2: Click “Add a site”, enter your DOCENT address (e.g. docent.your-org.edu), and choose the “Manual setup” / JS snippet option.
analyticsCard.step3: Cloudflare shows a short <script …> snippet. Copy the whole thing.
analyticsCard.step4: Paste it into the box below and press Save. Your visitor stats then appear back on the Cloudflare dashboard within a few minutes.
analyticsCard.snippetDescription: Paste the full snippet Cloudflare gives you (or just the token). Only the token is stored and used — the rest is ignored.
analyticsCard.tokenDetected: Token detected — analytics is live on every page.
analyticsCard.tokenNotFound: Couldn't find a Cloudflare token in that snippet. Paste the full <script … data-cf-beacon='{"token": "…"}'></script> Cloudflare gave you, or just the token itself.
analyticsCard.privacyNote: The beacon is cookieless and collects no personal data. DOCENT builds the tag itself from your token (it never runs the pasted HTML) and skips visitors who send Do Not Track.

importWizard.title: Import events from CSV
importWizard.uploadIntro: Upload a CSV of past events. Any reasonable spreadsheet works — DOCENT auto-detects common columns (title, date, venue, attendance, …) and recognises Symplectic Elements exports (their day-first dates are handled). You'll confirm the column mapping, then review each row before anything is saved.
importWizard.noRows: That file parsed, but contained no data rows.
importWizard.detectedSymplectic: Recognised a Symplectic Elements export with {{count}} rows. Dates are read day-first (UK style).
importWizard.detectedGeneric: Read {{count}} rows. Check the column mapping below, then start the review.
importWizard.mappingHelp: Each event field was matched to a CSV column automatically — fix any that were guessed wrong. Your mapping is applied when you start the review. Unmapped fields are simply left blank on every row (you can still fill them in per event).
importWizard.dateUnparsedWarning: Couldn't read the date {{raw}} from the CSV — pick it manually below.
importWizard.venueFromCsv: From the CSV: “{{name}}”{{city}} — pick the matching venue above, or create it.
importWizard.sameDayTitle: Already in DOCENT on this day
importWizard.sameDayNeedsDate: Pick a date to check for events already recorded that day.
importWizard.sameDayNone: Nothing recorded on {{date}} yet — no duplicates to worry about.

admin.title: Admin
admin.registrationDescription: New accounts require this access code. Share it only with people you want to let in; clear it to close sign-up entirely. The contact email is shown on the login and register pages so people know where to request a code or a password reset.
admin.communityNameDescription: Shown in the header, on the login page, and on the public impact page. Empty = plain DOCENT branding.
admin.publicImpactPageDescription: Serve a read-only summary of your community's impact (totals, charts, recent activity — never private notes or names) at <link>/impact</link>. Anyone with the link can view it.
admin.memberDirectoryDescription: Let any signed-in user browse the member directory (schools attended, languages spoken) — not just admins. Admins can always see it.
admin.loginMessageDescription: Optional announcement shown on the login page — a welcome note, a maintenance notice, whatever your community needs to see before signing in. Supports basic Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, [links](https://…), lists). Leave blank to show nothing.
admin.mapStartingPointDescription: Where the Map page centers on first load, before anyone pans around. Defaults to Tennessee.
admin.basemapDescription: The map imagery behind the markers, used by the Map page and by the map in PDF reports. The default needs no API key. To use CARTO, Stadia or MapTiler, paste their tile URL including your own key.
admin.basemapLightDescription: Must include {z}, {x} and {y}. Optional: {s} for subdomains, {r} for retina tiles. Leave empty for the default.
admin.basemapDarkDescription: Optional. Leave empty to reuse the light tiles inverted for dark mode.
admin.basemapAttributionDescription: Shown on the map and in report captions. Most providers require you to keep this visible.
admin.basemapMonochromeDescription: Desaturates the tiles so the coloured markers stand out. Turn off if your tiles are already a flat, muted style.
admin.mergeModalDescription: All of {{name}}'s events and venues move to the account you pick, then {{name}}'s account is deleted. This can't be undone.
admin.deactivatedUsersNote: Deactivated users can no longer log in, but their events stay in the community record.
admin.tempPasswordBody: Share this one-time password with <bold>{{name}}</bold> over a secure channel. They should log in and change it from their profile. It is shown only once.
admin.loginHistorySubtitle: Sign-ins and new accounts over the last 30 days.
admin.bannerMessageDescription: Shown at the top of every page for signed-in users. Leave blank to hide.

federationCard.title: Federation
federationCard.description: Share this instance's activity feed with sibling communities, and pull their activities into your merged views.
federationCard.publishToggleDescription: Serve this instance's activity feed so sibling communities can subscribe to it.
federationCard.feedUrlHelp: Hand this URL to sibling communities so they can pull your activities. It contains a secret token, so share it privately and only over HTTPS.
federationCard.tokenRotated: Feed token rotated. Re-share the new URL with your sibling communities.
federationCard.setSiteUrlHint: Publishing is on, but your feed URL isn't absolute yet. Set this instance's Site URL in the site-address settings so sibling communities get a complete, linkable URL.
federationCard.peersSectionDescription: Subscribe to sibling communities' feeds. Their activities are merged into your map and stats.
federationCard.confirmRemove: Remove sibling community "{{label}}"? Activities pulled from it will no longer appear in your merged views.
federationCard.rotateModalBody: This immediately invalidates your current feed URL. Every sibling community that reads your data will stop syncing and break until you send them the new URL and they update their setup. Only do this if the current token may have been exposed — it can't be undone.
federationCard.publishPlannedDescription: Also share upcoming (planned) events, so sibling communities can see your schedule. Off by default.
federationCard.tagFilterDescription: Leave empty to pull all of this sibling's events. Add tags to pull only events carrying at least one of them.
